definition: The number of requests, tokens, or predictions a system can process per unit of time.
details: Throughput and latency often trade off against each other; systems can be tuned (e.g., via batching) to prioritize one over the other depending on the application's requirements.
story: Picture a librarian organizing a million slips of paper so that any one of them can be found in a heartbeat. The examples a machine reads become the world it believes in. Better ingredients make a better meal, and the same is true here. Garbage in, garbage out — and the reverse: clean, representative data makes the model quietly brilliant. And that is Throughput — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
